title: How does laboratory accreditation and site-visit remediation work?

nodes.label: Submit application
nodes.detail: Upload the laboratory quality manual, proficiency test history, and application fee.

nodes.label: Dossier complete?
nodes.detail: Staff verify all required SOPs and proficiency records are attached.

nodes.label: Request missing docs
nodes.detail: Applicant has 30 days to upload missing SOPs before the application expires.

nodes.label: Upload revised dossier
nodes.detail: Provide the requested documents to resume desk review.

nodes.label: Assign assessor team
nodes.detail: Staff match conflict-free technical assessors to the lab's test disciplines.

nodes.label: Confirm site readiness
nodes.detail: Confirm dates and prepare instrument calibration records for inspection.

nodes.label: Conduct on-site audit
nodes.detail: Assessors observe bench testing and audit traceability records.

nodes.label: Any deficiencies?
nodes.detail: Assessors classify findings as none, minor CAPA, or major non-conformance.

nodes.label: Submit CAPA plan
nodes.detail: Lab submits root-cause corrective actions and evidence for each deficiency.

nodes.label: CAPA verified?
nodes.detail: Lead assessor reviews corrective evidence or requests a focused follow-up.

nodes.label: Committee grant
nodes.detail: Accreditation committee ratifies the report and issues the certificate.

nodes.label: Accredited lab
nodes.detail: Laboratory receives its accreditation seal and public directory listing.

cards.title: Standard accreditation track
cards.body: Complete dossier, 2-day site audit with no open deficiencies, and committee grant.

cards.title: Deficiencies & CAPA
cards.body: Labs have 60 days after the exit briefing to submit corrective action evidence.
